title: A Battle without Gun and Smoke: The Confrontation with Ebola

limitations: All 47 pages reviewed through contact sheets and rendered pages.
OCR damages Greek symbols and indexed rates; visual equations are authoritative.
The source uses simplified country, route, and production assumptions.

task_reconstruction.source: Summary, Introduction, Sections 4-11, and stakeholder letter
deliverables: Fit baseline and hospital-extended Ebola propagation models.
Predict country cases and deaths where data allow.
Choose delivery regions and centers using clustering, fairness, and efficiency.
Design TSP routes and a country delivery algorithm.
Estimate medicine production speed, urgency allocation, total quantity, and intervention sensitivity.
task_reconstruction.reconstruction_limit: No separate official problem statement was included; author prose reconstructs deliverables and never reclassifies path-derived A.

section_map.summary: Three ordered contributions: propagation, delivery, and medicine supply.
Context, task definitions, and five-part decomposition.
SEIIRF, parameter fitting, hospital extension, and country curves.
Production, allocation, integral demand, control factors.

contributions.summary: Genetic algorithm plus least squares updates epidemic parameters.
Hospital compartments and transmission rates improve curve fit.
Road-distance grouping reduces candidate delivery locations.
TSP and an iterative route-feasibility algorithm produce country routes.
Linear manufacturing, urgency allocation, and integration estimate 3400 units.

edges: MU-A-2015-34317-001 -> MU-A-2015-34317-002: baseline trajectories provide the calibration target
MU-A-2015-34317-002 -> MU-A-2015-34317-003: fitted parameters seed the hospital extension
MU-A-2015-34317-003 -> MU-A-2015-34317-004: country-specific advanced curves support forecasts
MU-A-2015-34317-004 -> MU-A-2015-34317-006: epidemic demand informs weighted location criteria
MU-A-2015-34317-006 -> MU-A-2015-34317-008: selected centers enter the integrated delivery algorithm
MU-A-2015-34317-007 -> MU-A-2015-34317-008: route model supplies feasible transport
MU-A-2015-34317-008 -> MU-A-2015-34317-010: delivery system is evaluated with operational scenarios
MU-A-2015-34317-003 -> MU-A-2015-34317-010: hospital and funeral pathways become sensitivity factors

feedbacks: Baseline fit failure motivates parameter refresh and hospital extension.
Sensitivity and weaknesses bound policy interpretation.
dependency_graph.closure_status: Epidemic model -> demand -> centers -> routes -> manufacturing -> control; no external operational validation.

assumptions.summary: Construction and storage cost are omitted for urgency.
Rare medicine and vaccine output increases linearly.
Vaccine is ignored in quantity calculation because susceptible population is much larger.
Countries are modeled separately; a no-boundary extension is future work.

data_and_preprocessing.summary: WHO cumulative cases and deaths are used for parameter fitting.
Sierra Leone hospital infection share motivates added parameters.
Provincial capitals and road-network distances enter clustering.
Country maps and route distances support delivery selection.

models.summary: H1/H2 pathways and modified infection terms.

verification.summary: Baseline curves compared to WHO data and fail at later horizon.
Hospital extension is compared with country curves.
Perturbed parameters and production speed are plotted.

results_trace.summary: Guinea reaches about 4000 total and 2500 deaths by 180 days in the scenario.
Country-specific locations and routes are selected.
The paper claims eradication in 50 days under its production scenario.

writing_logic.summary: Mission -> three ordinal contributions -> intervention outcome.
Baseline -> fit failure -> genetic refresh -> hospital extension -> country fit.
Emergency properties -> assumptions -> clustering -> fairness/efficiency -> routes.
State effects -> production law -> allocation -> integral demand -> controls.
Audience -> model evidence -> locations/routes -> quantity and speed.

language_observations.summary: Ordinal First/Second/Third transitions route the entire paper.
Failed fit is stated before new parameters and hospital mechanisms.
Definitions and assumptions precede clustering and route equations.
Overall results replay the model staircase and return to a time-bound decision.

judge_relevance_hypotheses.summary: Visible model-to-decision trace and quantitative route/supply outputs may aid auditability; award status is not causal proof.

weaknesses.summary: Baseline long-horizon fit fails after the calibration interval.
Many coupled parameters may reduce sensitivity and identifiability.
Construction, storage, capacity, and political costs are omitted.
Solver settings, vehicle capacities, and route uncertainty are incomplete.
Linear production and unit-dose assumptions are idealized.
50-day eradication and WMA recommendations lack external validation.

independent_extensions.summary: Add coverage, cross-border flows, capacity, storage, and road-time uncertainty to a joint facility-route optimization.
Re-estimate country models with held-out data, joint uncertainty, and replicated global sensitivity.

unresolved_questions: Genetic-algorithm seeds, population, mutation, stopping rule, and bounds are not reported.
Hospital parameter identifiability and country-specific calibration data are incomplete.
Road-distance matrix, clustering ties, center scalarization, and TSP solver settings are not reproducible.
Vehicle capacities, inventory balance, storage, and time windows are omitted.
Medicine units are a proxy and the vaccine is ignored in the quantity calculation.
One-factor sensitivity and 50-day eradication claims have no confidence intervals or external validation.
